transcript.text: My Panasonic NN-ST45KWBPQ is sparking inside when I heat soup, little blue flashes on the right-hand wall and a crackling noise. I stopped it. Is it safe?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Stop using the microwave now: switch it off at the socket and unplug it, and don't run it again (not even empty) until we know why it sparked. Never take the outer casing off — parts inside can hold a lethal charge even when it is unplugged. It is not safe to use the microwave again. The blue flashes and crackling indicate arcing, which can damage the internal high-voltage components or start a fire. You must unplug it immediately and do not attempt to run it. The most likely cause for sparks on the right-hand wall is a damaged waveguide cover (the small rectangular panel on the side of the cavity). This cover protects the antenna from food splashes; if it gets burnt, holed or cracked by arcing, electricity will jump across the gap. Other possibilities include a piece of metal or foil inside, or food debris causing an arc. Please perform this safe check: with the microwave unplugged and cool, open the door and remove all items. Look closely at that right-hand wall panel (the waveguide cover). If you see any black marks, holes, burns or cracks on it, do not try to fix it yourself. The appliance needs a qualified engineer to replace the cover and check the internal components for damage.

I've unplugged it and had a look. The cardboard-like panel on the right wall has a black burnt spot with greasy splatter on it. There was a slight burnt smell, and once a wisp of smoke came from that spot before it stopped when I turned it off. What should I do about it?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Because the waveguide cover is burnt and has caused arcing, you must not use the microwave again. A qualified engineer needs to replace the cover and inspect the internal cavity for any damage to the paint or other components that may have occurred during the sparking. Do not attempt to fix it yourself.
